newsitem.title: USA: New York Control Board approves $1.3 bln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: New York Control Board approves $1.3 bln of bonds.

text.p: The New York State Public Control Board has approved a total of nearly $1.28 billion of large bond offerings for various projects.
The following list provides the details of the bigger offerings, which were approved on February 12.
--Dormitory Authority, a maximum of $800 million of bonds for the Mental Health Facilities, to finance construction and refund selected 1987 revenue bonds.

--Environmental Facillities Corp, a maximum of $168.7 million of bonds, to be matched by $83.65 million of federal and state funds. The revenue bonds will be used to finance water pollution control projects for about 22 localities. The largest loans will be for:
--New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority, $75 million, Saratoga County, $18.2 million, Westchester County, $24.5 million, Town of Hempstead, $15 million,

--Public Benefit Corporations, including, Environmental Facilities Corp, Taxable State Service Contract Revenue Bonds, a maximum of $60 million. The issues will repay the state for certain sums contributed as the state's matching share of the State Water Pollution Control Revolving Fund.
--New York State Mortgage Agency, $50 million of tax-exempt refunding bonds, $100,000 million of new money bonds (tax-exempt), and $10 million of new money bonds (taxable).

--New York State Energy Research and Development Authority, $4 million of taxable bond proceeds, and $16 million of tax-exempt bond proceeds. Of the total, $18.3 million would be used for costs incurred at the Western New York Nuclear Service Center and to pay for some associated costs.
--Dormitory Authority, a maximum of $37 million of bonds for Siena College, to refund certain issues.
--Dormitory Authority, a maximum of $27 million of bonds for the Fairport Baptist Homes, FHA-insured mortgage nurshing home revenue bonds.
--Dormitory Authority, a maximum of $20 million of bonds for New York University, to buy equipment of its medical center.
--Dormitory Authority, a maximum of $19.5 million of bonds for New York City, to build a diagnostic and treatment center in Jamaica, the Merrick Center.
